title: Ensure 'ChatMCP' is set to 'Disabled'
description: This policy setting controls integration with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. The recommended state for this setting is: Disabled. Rationale: Integration with third-party MCP servers may result in unintended disclosure of information to the party running the server. Audit reads the Group Policy registry value and prints 'compliant', 'unset' (policy not configured, reported as FAIL) or the non-compliant value. Registry value: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode:ChatMCP (REG_DWORD); compliant when it is 0. Remediation writes 0 locally; in a domain set it through the ADMX so Group Policy does not revert it.
reference: CIS Visual Studio Code GPO Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.1 Ensure 'ChatMCP' is set to 'Disabled'

remediation.command: $p = 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode'; if (-not (Test-Path -Path $p)) { New-Item -Path $p -Force | Out-Null }; New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name 'ChatMCP' -Value 0 -PropertyType DWord -Force | Out-Null

title: Ensure 'ChatToolsAutoApprove' is set to 'Disabled'

Rationale: Automatic activation of agent mode tools may result in inadvertent disclosure of sensitive data to third-party servers backing the chat tool or unexpected modification to project files. Registry value: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode:ChatToolsAutoApprove (REG_DWORD); compliant when it is 0. Remediation writes 0 locally; in a domain set it through the ADMX so Group Policy does not revert it.

title: Ensure 'AllowedExtensions' is configured
description: This policy setting configures a list of extension selectors that determine which extensions are allowed or blocked. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled with a list of allowed extensions. Rationale: Allowing users to install any extension may result in unintended information disclosure to third parties, or the installation of malware. The benchmark marks this recommendation Manual (organisation-specific value or not reliably checkable), so it is reported as SKIP with review steps.
reference: CIS Visual Studio Code GPO Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2.1 Ensure 'AllowedExtensions' is configured

audit.command: Confirm via Group Policy (gpresult /h or the GPMC) that Computer Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Visual Studio Code\Extensions\AllowedExtensions is configured as the title requires. This group policy setting is backed by the following registry location with a REG_SZ value containing a JSON string. Registry: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode:AllowedExtensions

remediation.command: Configure through Group Policy: Computer Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Visual Studio Code\Extensions\AllowedExtensions = Enabled along with a JSON string defining the approved extensions

title: Ensure 'UpdateMode' is set to 'Enabled: Enable Automatic Update Checks. Code will check for updates automatically and periodically.'
description: This policy setting controls whether VS Code automatically updates when a new version is released. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled: Enable Automatic Update Checks. Code will check for updates automatically and periodically. Rationale: Software needs to be patched regularly to address vulnerabilities. Audit reads the Group Policy registry value and prints 'compliant', 'unset' (policy not configured, reported as FAIL) or the non-compliant value. Registry value: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode:UpdateMode (REG_SZ); compliant when it is 'default' (whitespace-insensitive). Remediation writes default locally; in a domain set it through the ADMX so Group Policy does not revert it.
reference: CIS Visual Studio Code GPO Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4.1 Ensure 'UpdateMode' is set to 'Enabled: Enable Automatic Update Checks. Code will check for updates automatically and periodically.'

remediation.command: $p = 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode'; if (-not (Test-Path -Path $p)) { New-Item -Path $p -Force | Out-Null }; New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name 'UpdateMode' -Value 'default' -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null

title: Ensure 'EnableFeedback' is set to 'Disabled'
description: This policy setting controls feedback mechanisms, such as the issue reporter and surveys. The recommended state for this setting is: Disabled. Rationale: The VS Code issue reporter can be configured to submit context such as basic system configuration and application settings. This may inadvertently disclose information that some organizations consider confidential. Audit reads the Group Policy registry value and prints 'compliant', 'unset' (policy not configured, reported as FAIL) or the non-compliant value. Registry value: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode:EnableFeedback (REG_DWORD); compliant when it is 0. Remediation writes 0 locally; in a domain set it through the ADMX so Group Policy does not revert it.

title: Ensure 'TelemetryLevel' is set to 'Enabled: off'
description: This policy setting controls telemetry for VS Code and extensions. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled: off. Rationale: Enabling this feature sends data to Microsoft and potentially third-party extension developers, which could lead to sensitive data being exposed. Audit reads the Group Policy registry value and prints 'compliant', 'unset' (policy not configured, reported as FAIL) or the non-compliant value. Registry value: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode:TelemetryLevel (REG_SZ); compliant when it is 'off' (whitespace-insensitive). Remediation writes off locally; in a domain set it through the ADMX so Group Policy does not revert it.
reference: CIS Visual Studio Code GPO Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3.2 Ensure 'TelemetryLevel' is set to 'Enabled: off'

remediation.command: $p = 'Registry::HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode'; if (-not (Test-Path -Path $p)) { New-Item -Path $p -Force | Out-Null }; New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name 'TelemetryLevel' -Value 'off' -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
